correctness.rationale: Four exact disjoint rational intervals map strictly into one another uniformly for 0.9978<=c<=0.9982; interval 2 has an exact concavity/completion-of-square bound. The cubic derivative has absolute value <4 on [0,1] and <1/100 on interval 2, so the four-step return is a strict 16/25 contraction on interval 0. The contraction theorem and disjoint intervals establish a primitive attracting four-cycle for each real control; the uncountable claim is analytic. Exact rational fractions in verify.py checked strict inequalities and derivative endpoints, not used in place of infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The full accessible 2021 five-page conference manuscript and the 2023 expanded journal article establish and numerically assess the exact cubic family, but do not give the stated attracting period-four parameter interval or uniform cycle-box certificate. Exact-family database and literature searches found no implication from the closest maps (stochastic logistic response, rational logistic superattraction, piecewise coupled logistic, binary16 state graphs). This is best-knowledge original relative to these inspected sources, not a claim of global priority.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently worded prior discovery of the same 4-cycle window may exist; database search is not novelty proof.
The 2021 conference date is 2021-11-28 to 2021-12-01; exact initial online upload day of its manuscript was not verified.
The interval certified is not necessarily the full stable window; there may be other invariant sets.

value.rationale: The originating papers motivate this specific simple map by widened uninterrupted chaotic behavior and employ finite-resolution numerical diagnostics. A rationally certified parameter interval with an attracting primitive period-four orbit is a nontrivial, positive-measure obstruction to uniformly nonperiodic dynamics, and local negative Lyapunov behavior is relevant to map-based signal generation. The claim is confined to a fixed published parameterization, not a fabricated general theorem or a cryptographic claim.
